title: 15 tips to get the best products on Temu
summary: 15 practical tips for buying well on Temu: judging listings, spotting poor quality, sizing, returns and paying safely. Shop smarter.
body_markdown:
I was scrolling through Temu a couple days ago and saw a really nice jacket that was fairly priced. As strong as I would like to think my will is, unfortunately I couldn’t resist, so it went in the cart, along with a new pair of gym shoes and a new phone case.


I got my first orders wrong because I just wasn't looking in the right place, and after getting burnt a few times, I’ve mastered the art of finding the perfect Temu order.


To get the best products on Temu, look at how many units a listing has sold rather than its star rating, read the specifications as well as the title, check buyer photos instead of studio images, and compare sizing charts against your own measurements. Stick to simple goods and avoid categories where quality varies most.


In the following paragraphs, I’ll be explaining in detail all you should know about getting exactly what you need on Temu.


## Before you buy: set expectations


Temu is a marketplace, which means the items in your cart come from many different sellers, not from one shop with a single standard. Quality therefore varies from listing to listing, and the same-looking product can be a pleasant surprise from one seller and a dud from another.


That has two practical effects.


- **Quality is uneven:** Low prices often indicate basic materials and light packaging. That is fine for a silicone spatula and risky for anything you need to last, fit perfectly, or plug into a wall.
- **Delivery depends on the warehouse:** Items shipped from overseas take longer than items shipped from a warehouse or seller near you, so the delivery estimate matters as much as the price.


Where Temu genuinely delivers value is on simple, low-risk goods: organisers, kitchen gadgets, phone accessories, craft supplies, and basic home items. If you want to know how its prices stack up against another big marketplace, read our comparison on[is Temu cheaper than AliExpress](https://grey.co/blog/is-temu-cheaper-than-aliexpress) .


The rest of this guide assumes that your goal is good-enough items at a fair price, with no nasty surprises.


## 15 tips for buying well on Temu


Each of these Temu shopping tips is something you can check on the listing page in under a minute. Together, they cover most of the ways a cheap order goes wrong.


### 1. Read the specification, not the title


Titles are written to match searches, so sometimes, they are stuffed with keywords. The specification section is where the real details live: material, dimensions, weight, capacity, and compatibility. If a listing has no specification at all, treat that as a warning.


### 2. Check how many units have sold


Many listings show a units-sold figure. A product that thousands of people have bought and kept has been tested far more than one with ten glowing reviews. Look at volume first, then at the rating.


### 3. Look at buyer photos, not studio images


Studio shots show the best-case scenario under perfect lighting. Buyer photos show the item on a real table, on a real body, in daylight. Scroll to the review photos before you look at anything else.


### 4. Run a reverse image search on the main photo


Press and hold the main image, or save it, then search it with a reverse image tool. If the same polished photo appears on many unrelated listings, it is probably a generic stock image, and buyer photos matter even more.


### 5. Compare the size chart with your own measurements


Sizing labels vary by seller, so “M” tells you very little. Measure a similar item that fits you well, then compare it with the centimetres or inches in the size chart, not the label.


### 6. Read the three-star and one-star reviews first


Five-star reviews tell you what the seller wants you to believe. Low and middling reviews usually name the actual problems: sizing, smell, a flimsy zip, a cable that stops charging. If the same complaint appears repeatedly, it’s most likely a problem.


### 7. Check dimensions properly


Be sure you’re getting the proper size, as it can sometimes be difficult to picture how big or smal things are. Take the stated length, width, or height and compare it with an object at home using a tape measure. A “30 cm” organiser is smaller than most people picture.


### 8. Look for specific materials


“Premium” and “high quality” mean nothing. “100% cotton”, “stainless steel”, or “BPA-free silicone” are claims you can check against the spec and the reviews. Vague wording often means the seller has nothing specific to claim.


### 9. Check the delivery estimate and where the item ships from


Some items ship from nearby, and others come from overseas. Look at the estimated delivery date and any local-warehouse label before you pay, especially for gifts or anything with a deadline.


### 10. Ignore the crossed-out price


Temu’s own terms of use tell shoppers not to rely on the strike-through price when deciding what to buy. Compare the price you would actually pay with similar listings instead.


### 11. Compare two or three similar listings


Search for the same item and open several results. Put the specifications, units sold, and buyer photos side by side. The cheapest listing is rarely the best, and the gap between it and the second-cheapest is often small.


### 12. Check whether the item can be returned


Temu’s returns page states that most items can be returned within 90 days of purchase, and that the first return on each order is free. Some items, such as underwear, groceries, and customised products, cannot be returned, so check the listing before you order.


### 13. Count the total, not the headline price


Temu’s terms state that listed prices exclude customs duties, sales taxes, and shipping, which are charged separately where applicable. Check the checkout total before you confirm, and do not pad your cart with filler just to reach a free-shipping threshold.


### 14. Start with one item


Before a big haul, order a single low-cost item from a seller. See how it arrives, how it feels, and how long delivery takes. Then decide whether to order more.


### 15. Photograph the item as soon as it arrives


Take photos of the item, the packaging, and any damage straight away. If you need a refund, clear evidence taken on delivery day makes your case much easier, and return windows start from the purchase date.


## Reading reviews and photos properly: how to spot fake reviews on Temu


Reviews help, but they are not proof, so treat them as clues and look for patterns.


**Buyer photos beat studio shots**
A real customer photo shows the colour, the finish, and the true size. If a listing has hundreds of reviews and almost no customer photos, be cautious.


**Volume beats a perfect rating**
A 4.4 from thousands of buyers tells you more than a 5.0 from a dozen. Small numbers are easy to skew.


**Watch for these patterns:**


- **Clusters:** The[FTC's guidance on evaluating online reviews](https://www.consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-evaluate-online-reviews) advises being wary of a sudden burst of reviews in a short window, so check the dates.
- **One-review accounts:** The same guidance says a reviewer who created an account to write a single review for one product may be fake.
- **Copy-and-paste praise:** Lines like “great product, fast delivery” repeated across reviews, with no detail, say little.
- **Four-star fakes:** Some fake positive reviews avoid the top score to look believable, so do not dismiss every moderate rating, and do not trust every high one.


**Look for detail**
The most useful reviews mention specific details, such as how a seam held up after washing, how long a battery lasted, and how the item compared with its photo. Mixed reviews that mention both pros and cons are usually more informative than pure praise.


Temu’s terms of use say reviews must be truthful and based on first-hand experience, and that sponsored reviews must be clearly marked, but they also allow Temu to remove reviews at its discretion. Use that as a reminder that you are the final check.


## What to buy on Temu and what to avoid


**Categories that tend to work**


- **Organisers and storage:** Boxes, hooks, and drawer dividers are simple objects with few ways to fail.
- **Kitchen gadgets:** Silicone tools, measuring spoons, and basic utensils, as long as the listing names the material.
- **Phone cases and stands:** Cheap to replace, and buyer photos show the fit.
- **Craft and stationery supplies:** Beads, stickers, notebooks, and pens are easy to judge from reviews.
- **Home and party decor:** Fairy lights are a common pick, though anything with a plug deserves extra care.


**Categories that often disappoint**


- **Anything that charges or plugs in:** Chargers, power banks, and cheap batteries are where poor quality costs the most, so consider established brands.
- **Items where fit matters:** Shoes, fitted clothing, and bras depend on sizing that varies by seller.
- **Skincare, supplements, and anything you swallow or apply:** Ingredient claims are hard to verify from a listing.
- **Children’s products:** Toys and baby items should meet safety standards you can check.
- **Brand lookalikes:** If a listing resembles a famous brand at a fraction of the price, expect it to be a copy.


None of this means every item in these groups is bad. It means mistakes cost more, and the savings are rarely worth the risk.


## Paying safely and without FX surprises


A good deal can still get expensive at the payment step. Prices on Temu are listed in dollars for US shoppers, and if your card is not a dollar card, your bank converts the amount and may add a foreign transaction fee or a weaker exchange rate. On a $9 order, the difference is small. Across a big haul, it adds up.

## Frequently asked questions


### How do I find good products on Temu?


Start with simple, low-risk items, then check the specifications, units sold, buyer photos, and the lower-rated reviews. Compare two or three similar listings, and order a single item first before a bigger purchase.


### Are the reviews real?


Some will be, and some may not be. The FTC says it can often be nearly impossible to tell for sure, so look for patterns such as bursts of reviews in a short window, one-review accounts, and copy-and-paste praise. Detailed reviews with buyer photos are the most useful.


### Will I pay customs?


Possibly. Temu’s terms state that listed prices exclude customs duties, sales taxes, and shipping, which are charged separately where applicable. The US duty-free treatment for low-value parcels was suspended for all countries from 29 August 2025, so check your checkout total. This is general guidance, not professional tax advice. Consult a certified tax professional for your specific situation.


### How do returns work?


Temu’s returns page says most items can be returned within 90 days of purchase, with the first return on each order free. Some items, including underwear, groceries, and customised products, cannot be returned. Refunds go to your original payment method or to a Temu credit balance, and bank refunds can take several business days. Check the listing for its exact terms.


### Is it safe to pay by card?


Card payments carry some risk anywhere online. Shop only in the official app or on the official site, check your statements, and consider using a virtual card funded with just the amount you need.
